t: You're thinking about the Waterloo Vase, a stone urn about fifteen feet tall that stands in the garden of Buckingham Palace. It was carved from a single piece of Carrara marble. It was first presented to Napoleon, who meant to have it carved to celebrate future victories. After his defeat at Waterloo, it passed to the Prince Regent, later George IV. He had the sculptor Richard Westmacott decorate it with reliefs celebrating that victory. It proved too heavy for its planned home at Windsor Castle, so it went to the National Gallery instead.
